item.title: ROUNDTABLE: What Inside NU is thankful for this Thanksgiving
item.description: Folks, happy Thanksgiving! We hope you’re enjoying a much-needed rest from what has been a hectic fall in Northwestern sports. We sure are! But, if you do find some time between playing backyard football and scarfing down some turkey (like many of us are currently indulging in), you should check out what we’re feeling thankful for this year! Once again, happy, happy Thanksgiving! Enjoy! Zac Penson Thankful for: The Ryan Family I could talk about the season Northwestern football started to have under David Braun and Chip Kelly, but after the disaster that the team has become after losing Aidan Chiles, the memory fans will take from this season is the one artifact that will stand as a colosseum on campus for decades to come: the new stadium. The incredible generosity from the Ryan Family is something that myself and ‘Cats fans (as well as probably the away fans that tend to fill our stadium) alike will take away from this season in the long run. It is just an absolutely beautiful stadium that will hopefully lead Northwestern down a path of successful recruitment and cement its place as a legitimate football contender in the Big Ten. If it weren’t for the generosity of the Ryan Family and specifically the effort Pat Ryan Jr. put into the stadium, we wouldn’t have the incredible new Wildcat Wall, the over the top lounges, incredible sight lines, open concourses, the Great Chicago Food Festival, Thunderstruck… the list could go on forever. For all of that, thank you, and Happy Thanksgiving ‘Cats fans! Donovan West Thankful for: Northwestern field hockey I’m not going to lie and say I’m the biggest Northwestern field hockey fan who watched every game this season. There are other diehards on Inside NU that have you covered in that aspect. However, I’m still thankful for our three-time national championship-winning ‘Cats. Not only because they have brought so much pride and glory to Evanston over the past couple of years, but also, selfishly, because it’s a good conversation starter at the Thanksgiving table. When my family asks about NU’s sports, or lack thereof, I run through the typical lowlights of men’s and women’s basketball as well as the head-spinning football and tragedy of Aiden Chiles, but am able to end with, “But hey, the field hockey team just won the National Championship.” So, I’m thankful for the ‘Cats for saving my Thanksgiving conversations. item.title: Cincinnati Bearcats beat Georgia in 1st game of ESPN Invitational
item.description: For Coach Jerrod Calhoun's new Cincinnati Bearcats roster, it was the first non-Ohio road game of the season. Playing in the ESPN Events Invitational at Disney's Wide World of Sports, UC held off Georgia of the Southeastern Conference on Thanksgiving, 83-81. It took a Jayden Hastings block of Georgia's James Scott, followed by his knocking the ball out of bounds for the victory. The Bulldogs made a furious comeback in the second half and the Bearcats had no field goals over the final 2:48. UC led by 16 at halftime and as many as 18 early in the second half, but Georgia came back to take a lead with 6:26 to go on a Kanon Catchings 3-pointer. An MJ Collins Jr. trey put the Bearcats up 75-72 with 3:57 to go and they would not trail from there. The Bearcats led for 31:26 of the 40 minutes. Myles Colvin had 23 points for the Bearcats, all in the first half and Tyler Tejada also finished with 23. Collins had 16 for UC. The Bearcats made just four triples in their last game vs. UMass Lowell . By halftime in Orlando, they were 10-for-14 from the arc. Their previous season-high was 10 in full, 40-minute contests vs. Green Bay and Dayton. UC finished12-for-22, so just 2-for 8 in the second half. They forced 13 Georgia turnovers, 10 in the first half and had nine steals, with eight in the first half. Georgia did dominate on the backboards, 46-33. WHO ELSE?? @mylesjcolvin has 20 and counting in the first half! https://t.co/kH5LUzapvd — Cincinnati Men’s Hoops (@GoBearcatsMBB) November 26, 2026 The Bearcats and Bulldogs played a non-conference game last year in Atlanta, with Georgia winning 84-65. The series lead now goes to UC's only other road game this season was Calhoun's 300th career coaching win at Dayton, 95-72. The Georgia game was another test for UC's 6-foot-10, 245-pound man-in-the-paint, Jayden Hastings. He played 14 minutes with six points, six rebounds and six blocks vs. UMass Lowell . Against the Bulldogs, Hastings had six points, eight rebounds and four blocks, including the game-winner. It was a return home for the senior from Orlando, who had an estimated 20 friends and family on hand. Next up, the Bearcats face his old team, Boston College. The Eagles and UCF battled Thanksgiving afternoon. After battling back from a shoulder injury, Hastings left the game with a bloody nose after being elbowed by Georgia's Donovan Williams on a flagrant foul. Calhoun also started Moeller High's Eric Mahaffey for the first time. Friday, Nov. 27 at 4:30 p.m. (Eastern), it's UC and Boston College on the ACC Network. The Eagles played UCF after UC's Thanksgiving game at Disney's Wide World of Sports. item.title: Contact made: Liverpool star wanted by European club
item.description: Contact made: Liverpool star wanted by European club Virgil van Dijk transfer latest as Trabzonspor make contact over Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk’s future has moved back into focus after fresh reports in Turkey suggested Trabzonspor have opened discussions over a possible deal for the Liverpool captain. According to Hassan Tuncel, there has been “first contact” involving a world-class central defender, with the information pointing towards Van Dijk and communication with his representatives. That development adds another layer to a situation that already feels finely balanced. Van Dijk signed a two-year extension in April 2025, taking his deal through to June 2027, yet uncertainty has persisted. The Dutch defender admitted recently that he has “no idea” where he will play next season, a line that naturally intensified interest across Europe and beyond. Trabzonspor move enters early stage The understanding from Turkey is that Trabzonspor are exploring whether a deal is possible, with an apparent preference on their side to try in the winter window. Van Dijk’s side, however, are thought to favour seeing out the season at Liverpool before any firm decision is taken. Other reports in the same market indicate the timing remains unresolved, with January and next summer both still under consideration. There is also background worth noting. Mohamed Salah joined Trabzonspor in August, with Fabinho following later that month, which has only heightened intrigue around another high-profile arrival. Separate claims have even suggested an offer may already have been put forward, while Van Dijk’s reported valuation stands at €20 million. Liverpool stance still central For now, Liverpool’s position remains the key factor. Van Dijk continues to play a major role at Anfield and recently completed the full 90 minutes in the 4-0 win over Manchester United. His standing inside the squad, his performance level and his leadership mean any decision is unlikely to be taken lightly. Since arriving from Southampton in January 2018, Van Dijk has made 391 appearances and helped deliver every major honour of this era, including two Premier League titles and the Champions League. Interest is understandable. Resolution, though, still appears some distance away. Our View This feels like one to watch calmly rather than one to panic over. Clubs making contact with a player of Van Dijk’s stature is hardly a shock, especially when he is 34 and every move from here carries huge significance. Trabzonspor will see an opportunity, particularly with familiar faces already there, and they are entitled to test the waters. The bigger point is whether Liverpool are ready to move on, and right now that feels far less certain. He is still playing, still leading, still setting standards. When a captain remains that influential, it is difficult to imagine the club rushing towards an exit unless all parties are aligned. There is also a sense that timing matters here. item.description: The Orlando Magic kicked off Thanksgiving by serving breakfast to hundreds of people at the Coalition for the Homeless of Central Florida. The Orlando Magic kicked off Thanksgiving by serving breakfast to hundreds of people at the Coalition for the Homeless of Central Florida. First-year head coach Sean Sweeney, who took the job in June, joined the volunteers. As is team tradition, he paid for the meal. That work includes the annual Orlando Wine Festival & Auction, which benefits the Orlando Magic Youth Foundation. “I think it’s very important,” Sweeney said. item.title: Hamilton and Leclerc Hold Fresh Discussions – Cannot Predict Every Scenario in Races
item.description: Lewis Hamilton said on Thursday at the Qatar Grand Prix that he and Charles Leclerc have held positive internal discussions since their Las Vegas collision, while admitting they cannot plan for every scenario in a race. Ferrari needed another set of discussions after the Las Vegas run-in between Hamilton and Leclerc. They held it in Qatar, and Hamilton called it positive. He didn’t share what was discussed, but said it was good for both sides. He spoke to reporters at Thursday’s media day (Nov. 26) in Lusail. Fresh Discussions After Las Vegas “We just had the internal discussions,” Hamilton said to the media. “No, everything stays internal. But good discussions. Positive, yeah. It’s been positive. Charles and I sat here earlier and had a good discussion as well.” Do we need a permanent solution? Yes. But Hamilton put it on Ferrari F1 team principal Frederic Vasseur for any solution. The Brit didn’t wish to add anything else, having already conveyed his thoughts multiple times in the last few weekends. “I mean, that’s for Fred to decide ultimately,” said Hamilton . “I have made my point clear already about them. So yeah, there’s not really much more to say about it really. I said my piece before, and my point hasn’t really changed.” In terms of predicting the scenarios, Hamilton reckons it is not possible to decide about everything for the Grand Prix. They discuss various situations pre-race, but a lot of times things don’t pan out the same way, and collisions still happen. Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc at the Las Vegas GP. Image Credit: Scuderia Ferrari Hamilton Says They Cannot Predict Every Scenario He made clear that he attacks as much as possible, but he is mindful of things, thinking about Ferrari always. “I mean, you can never cover everything because every scenario is different, but definitely you can go through every single race, corner by corner and discuss things that Charles and I have,” said Hamilton. “But yeah, I mean, there’s always going to be something new that you maybe haven’t foreseen, but also, you have to use your instinct, and … also, always the core of it has to be the team. Obviously, I mean, just speaking for myself- when I’m driving, when I’m attacking whoever is on track, I’m always thinking, okay, how is this going to impact everybody behind me, team-wise. “So, I really do try to be as responsible as I can and make the best decision when I am attacking, I think. We’re going to figure it out. We’re teammates at the end of the day, and I think we always learn. We do always learn through these experiences, while maybe it doesn’t necessarily look like it. “But there will be learnings that we take from this difficult period, and I still believe in everything we’re building and working towards in the background,” summed up Hamilton.

item.title: Philadelphia Eagles reporter writes bizarre four-word article on potential Aaron Rodgers signing
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers is back on the free-agent market after leaving the Pittsburgh Steelers, and speculation is building about where he could play next if he does not want to retire. item.title: Lewis Hamilton confirms "positive" talks with Charles Leclerc after Las Vegas clash
item.description: Motorsport photo Seven-time Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari's talks since the Las Vegas Grand Prix have been "positive", and believes he and his team-mate Charles Leclerc can move forward together after their latest clash. Leclerc spun Hamilton around while the team-mates fought over sixth place in Las Vegas, three weeks after another clash at the Mexican Grand Prix. Leclerc was given a 10-second penalty and finished 10th, while Hamilton recovered to seventh. Team principal Fred Vasseur called the incident "a lack of respect for the team", and said Ferrari's message after Mexico had been clear. Speaking to the media in Qatar, Hamilton would not go into detail about what had been said since, but made it clear the discussions had gone well. "Everything stays internal. But good discussions," he said. "Positive, yeah. It's been positive. Charles and I sat here earlier on and had a good discussion as well." Asked whether the pair could now move forward in harmony, Hamilton was clear. "I do. I do. We're going to figure it out. You know, we're team-mates at the end of the day, and we do always learn from these experiences, while maybe it doesn't necessarily look like it," he said. Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari "But there will be learnings that we take from this difficult period, and I still believe in everything we're building and working towards in the background." Hamilton said he and Leclerc had already been through every race "corner by corner", but admitted no plan could cover every situation on track. "You can never cover everything, because every scenario is different," he said. "There's always going to be something new that you maybe haven't foreseen. But also you have to use your instinct, and at the core of it, always have to have the team." He believes the difficult moments will make Ferrari stronger in the long run. "These are definitely very, very challenging times for Fred and Charles and I. But these are the moments that you really learn and grow closer together, through conversation and communicating and having those sit-downs," Hamilton said. The Briton also expects to stay in touch with Leclerc over the winter, when the pair are "out of competition" and Leclerc is settling into life as a new father. "I have no doubts that next year we'll come back working hard together and in a better place. We'll hopefully put better processes in place so that we can really elevate the team," he said. Caicedo was forced off in the first half of last weekend’s match against Leeds United, with his departure, combined with Leeds’ equalizer, resulting in the Blues completely losing our ways and going on to suffer (yet another) rather embarrassing home defeat against historic rivals. “Yes [he’s been able to train], he’s going to be OK for tomorrow.” Unfortunately, the likes of João Pedro and Maxence Lacroix remain out and without a specific timetable for their return. Lacroix’s absence will likely result in yet another game for Wesley Fofana, who continues to frustrate with every appearance, including a recent appearance on a podcast. The reaction to some of the things he said during that 2-hour interview has been less than positive, especially the part where he talked about his performance against Liverpool in the League Cup. But unlike many fans, Alonso considers the case closed now. Fofana apparently apologized for what he said, how he said it, and when he said it. Lesson learned? We’ll have to wait and see. “We have addressed that with him and for sure it was unfortunate. He apologised, he knows it was not right the moment, it was not right the content, we are here to take things seriously and he said that it’s not going to be repeated and we know that it’s something that we don’t want, these kind of things and they are not going to be repeated for sure. [The case is] closed.” -Xabi Alonso; source: Football.London So I guess it’s a question of choosing the least worst option between Fofana and Levi Colwill, who’s had his fair share of terrible outings, plus youngsters like Josh Acheampong or Aarón Anselmino or Olutayo Subuloye. They all have plenty of promise but come with the usual caveats regarding young and inexperienced players. (It would be great if we had some proper veterans to play alongside them, but alas.)

item.title: Maple Leafs Make Significant Changes To Power Play With Marchenko Return
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect He’s baaack. Kirill Marchenko has been desperately missed by the Toronto Maple Leafs over the past month. That’s an understatement. Whether it be 5-on-5 or on the power play, injecting his energy and skill should help a moribund Toronto offense. Granted, looking at Jim Hiller’s practice lines for even strength means absolutely nothing in this Leafs season, as the often-confused coach puts his lines through a blender from nearly the opening puck drop in each and every game. But when it comes to the power play, the way they work on the special teams unit at practice often does translate to the games. And on Thursday, there’s been a significant change to the first power play unit. Kirill Marchenko will immediately rejoin the group as he returns to the lineup for Friday afternoon’s game in Boston. But, as shocking as this may come to followers of the Leafs this season, it will not come at the expense of young Gavin McKenna. No, Marchenko’s placement on PP1 will bump William Nylander off the unit. Accountability is a beautiful thing. https://t.co/vFjR7VOt4s — Nick Alberga (@thegoldenmuzzy) November 26, 2026 As you can imagine, no, Willie is not pleased about the move. “I told him I didn’t agree with it, but that’s okay,” said Nylander. Nylander’s play of late has Leafs Nation up in arms. He hasn’t scored a goal in eight games, is a minus-6 through that period, and has just three points. Then there was the egregious giveaway right out in front of the net in the recent loss to the Columbus Blue Jackets. To his old linemate Matthew Knies, no less. Nylander with an absolute muffin delivery to the former Leaf Knies. No one cares less than William Nylander in Toronto right now What is this pass 😂😂 #Leafs pic.twitter.com/Us4YRujqPm — RGF (@rgfray1) November 22, 2026 Nylander feels his egregious giveaway 2 games ago has led to his demotion Apparently, Nylander believes his demotion to the second power play unit is punishment for that turnover. Hiller responded by saying it’s about making Nylander the “focal point” of the second unit, per Jonas Siegel . Yet somehow, despite that brutal giveaway two games ago, Nylander was still out there being trusted in the final minutes of their first win in 10 games the other night. McKenna, who had actually scored the game-winner midway through the third period, was benched for the rest of that game. There’s simply no figuring out what’s going on in the mind of Jim Hiller. Most of the time, from the puzzling looks and answers he gives the media to some of his moves, it doesn’t seem like Hiller knows what’s going on in there, either. We’ll see how long this new power play arrangement lasts. With Hiller, and with Nylander, anything is possible. item.title: John Harbaugh’s Verdict: Abdul Carter May Play Sunday
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Abdul Carter missed Wednesday’s practice, which sent a wave of worry through the Giants’ locker room and the fanbase. The edge rusher was seen working on a side field with a trainer instead of running with the main group. ESPN’s Jordan Raanan posted on X that Carter was “not in uniform working on a side field with a trainer. Something to keep an eye on.” The same report noted that defensive lineman Shelby Harris and cornerback Dru Phillips also skipped the session. Fans feared a potential blow to the defense just days before a crucial matchup on the road. John Harbaugh quickly shut down the panic with a clear update that the team needed to hear. The head coach told reporters that Carter’s issue is minor and that the player is “day-to-day.” Harbaugh added a definitive line that changes the entire outlook for Sunday: “He should be fine for the game.” This statement comes after Carter was named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for his two-sack performance against Jacksonville. The Timing of the Injury Report The Giants have played 10 games so far this season, and Carter has been a consistent force with 26 tackles and four sacks. His ability to generate pressure is vital for a defense that has climbed to the top of the NFC East. Missing a midday practice is often a smart move to preserve a player for the actual game. Harbaugh knows that a full practice session does not guarantee a better outcome than resting a key piece. The coach emphasized that mid-November is the time to get ready for the games that truly matter. A Critical Matchup in Indianapolis The Giants travel to Lucas Oil Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 29, to face the Indianapolis Colts. The Colts are 3-8, and New York is a heavy favorite to beat them. However, the Giants must avoid a “trap game” mentality after their recent upset win. Harbaugh has warned his team that they cannot get carried away by the victory over Jacksonville. The defense needs Carter at full strength to maintain the pressure that has defined their play this month. Carter’s injury status remains a key detail to watch as the team prepares for the road trip. While the coach says he should be fine, the final decision rests on how his ankle and calf feel during the week. Per Sports Illustrated , Carter is listed with ankle and calf issues on the injury report.

(Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty Although Jeremiah Trotter Jr. landed plenty of praise for his progress throughout the offseason with the Philadelphia Eagles, it wasn’t clear that he would become a key player for the defense in 2026. At the start of the season, the Eagles were more focused on Zack Baun and the development of the former first-round pick, Jihaad Campbell. But as Trotter continued to thrive, he couldn’t be denied. Sure, setbacks helped him get more opportunities than expected, but he made it difficult for the Eagles to take him off the field. Pro Football Focus’ rundown of grades for top linebackers in the league this season suggests that the Eagles potentially have a budding star in their 2024 fifth-round pick. His snaps were limited to just 35% in two out of the next three games, but then Trotter played in at least 90% of the defensive snaps over the past three games. This season, Trotter has 64 tackles, with three going for a loss. He got to the quarterback with two hits and landed a half-sack. With Zack Baun out for at least four games, Trotter won’t be going anywhere as long as he’s healthy. He’ll get a chance to keep building and show the Eagles that he was a steal of a pick at No. 155 out of Clemson in 2024. item.title: A flurry of pitcher signings around MLB
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 30: Kevin Gausman #12 of the Chicago Cubs reacts in the National League Wild Card game against the San Diego Padres at Petco Park on September 30, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Matt Dirksen/Chicago Cubs/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we creep closer to the seemingly inevitable MLB lockout that will start at 11 p.m. Central on December 1, 2026, we are seeing a flurry of free agent activity, with teams snatching up starting pitchers, in particular. This year’s free agent class, outside of Tarik Skubal, is pretty uninspiring, low on star power and heavy on middle-class options. Those middle-class options are starting to fly off the board, though. Kevin Gausman, who just wrapped up a five year deal he signed with the Toronto Blue Jays prior to the 2022 season (the final two months of which had him as a member of the Chicago Cubs), reportedly agreed to a 1 year, $25 million deal with the Detroit Tigers. The righthander, who turns 36 in January, was generally expected to get a short-term deal for a lesser annual average value. Gausman provides durability and gets a lot of ground balls, and he is getting more than the $22 million AAV he commanded in his deal with Toronto. Whether this is betting on himself to rebound after putting up a 4.51 ERA — his first 4+ ERA since pre-pandemic — or both player and team being uncertain of what the landscape under a new CBA will look like, and thus giving themselves max flexibility, who is to say. The Colorado Rockies, meanwhile, appear to be trying to corner the market on mid starting pitchers. They reportedly have agreed to terms with David Peterson on a two year, $32 million deal, and with Patrick Sandoval on a three year, $42 million deal. Peterson was projected by Ben Clemens of Fangraphs and Kiley McDaniel of ESPN to land one year deals in the low-teens, while MLB Trade Rumors and the Fangraphs crowdsource median each projected two years at $11-12 million. Peterson got the high end of the range on years and still comfortably exceeded the annual average value projected. The 31 year old 2017 first rounder has posted remarkably consistent xERAs the past four seasons ranging from 4.59 to 4.92, despite a 2.90 ERA and 2024 and a 3.48 FIP in 2025 that produced spikes those years in his bWAR and fWAR, respectively. Like Gausman, he was traded to the Cubs mid-season, and posted a 3.70 ERA for Chicago, compared to a 6.09 ERA for the Mets. His 4.56 xERA for the Cubs was not much better than the 4.97 xERA he put up for the Mets, however, and his 4.06 Cubs FIP was actually worse than his 3.85 FIP for the Mets. Peterson strikes out a below average number of batters and walks an above average number of batters. However, he generates a lot of ground balls, and so maybe the Rockies feel like he’s a better fit in the thin area and big outfield of Coors Field. item.title: Wild NFL Proposal Sends Aaron Rodgers to Packers to End Career in Green Bay
item.description: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - JANUARY 08: Aaron Rodgers #12 of the Green Bay Packers warms up prior to the game against the Detroit Lions at Lambeau Field on January 08, 2023 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) Getty Aaron Rodgers has only a few weeks left in his NFL career, and one analyst suggests he could go back to where it all started. The Pittsburgh Steelers cut Rodgers loose on Wednesday, capping off a wild and unpredictable 17-hour stretch that started with a late-night announcement that he was being benched. Rodgers then aired the team’s dirty laundry in an interview with Pat McAfee, leveling allegations that head coach Mike McCarthy would fall asleep in meetings and referred to the team as the Packers. Aaron Rodgers Return to Green Bay? Rodgers is expected to clear waivers, where he would be free to sign with any NFL team. That could include a return trip to the Packers, Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox suggested. In an article breaking down the landing spots for Rodgers, Knox listed the Packers as a “break glass” emergency option if starter Jordan Love were to get hurt. Knox noted that Rodgers and the Packers had their own messy breakup, but suggested it wasn’t due to the current regime. “Should the Packers lose starter Jordan Love to injury, a homecoming would make tons of sense for Rodgers and for Green Bay,” Knox wrote. “Rodgers’ first stint didn’t end particularly well, and he essentially forced the Packers to trade him to New York. However, he did spend four seasons under head coach Matt LaFleur and knows his offense well. “Rodgers won a pair of league MVP awards in LaFleur’s system.” While it would require a season-ending injury to Love to make the reunion happen, the Packers might be desperate enough to consider signing Rodgers in that scenario. Green Bay has a very difficult route to the playoffs after losing to the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday, dropping their record to 6-5. The Packers may need to win out in order to reach the postseason, and even 12-5 might require tiebreakers given the number of strong teams in their division and NFC West. Aaron Rodgers Could Have More Sensible Option Rodgers could find a more immediate market once he hits free agency, Knox suggested. He noted that the New England Patriots are expected to scan the quarterback market for help after Drake Maye suffered what could be a season-ending injury. “Rodgers is now a part of that market, and his ability to read defenses, make smart decisions, and throw in rhythm would mesh with Josh McDaniels’ offense,” Knox wrote. “While Rodgers has no experience with McDaniels or head coach Mike Vrabel, he does have a history with receivers coach Todd Downing.” Rodgers could also opt to take an early retirement, as he had said prior to the start of the season that this would be his final one in the NFL. item.title: Stephen A. Smith calls out the NFL after what he saw during Packers’ loss to the Rams
item.description: Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images Fans may have forgotten that there is actually football being played in the NFL amid the media storm that has been created by Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. Wednesday night saw the Los Angeles Rams leapfrog the Seattle Seahawks to the second spot in the NFC West with their victory over the Green Bay Packers. It was a convincing win for Sean McVay’s team, who have finally found their form following the turbulent start to the year. Although focus has quickly reverted back to the situation in Pittsburgh, Stephen A. Smith was keen to vent his frustrations surrounding Kamren Kinchens’ ejection at SoFi Stadium. The ESPN analyst was baffled by the decision to throw the Rams’ safety out of the game. Stephen A. Smith left furious by Kamren Kinchens’ ejection in Rams victory Packers wide receiver Christian Watson suffered a concussion following a big hit from Kinchens. The officials deemed the hit was to the head of the wideout, despite the safety leading with his shoulder. “I don’t agree with that. I did not agree that warranted an ejection or anything like that. I know my brother Ray Lewis is losing his mind, because he’s like, ‘D*** it, we’re men! What are they doing?’ You know, taking everything away from them when it comes to the defence and what it’s allowed to do,” Smith said on First Take. “Do we have that footage of that hit? Do y’all have that? Show that to us, please. Tell me where the illegal hit is on this. What is this? That would seem like a good one to me. Look at that. Come on y’all, right in the shoulders! What’s up? I mean, why is that an ejection? Why?” “It was on the left shoulder, and it was just a devastating hit. He caught the ball, he was in bounds, and I hit him on the shoulder. I just put a hat on him, you know, let him know. I mean, I saw no problem with that hit, zero. At the very least it’s a penalty, not an ejection. I’m like, what are they talking about? It landed on his shoulder. He just got popped silly, that’s all.” The level of officiating has come under real scrutiny this season. This is not even the first time this week that NFL fans have been left frustrated by the referees. Fans were baffled by the Cincinnati Bengals being penalised on Monday night after Joe Burrow was hit late by a Washington Commanders defender. This incident, in particular, only highlights the emphasis the league is putting on protecting so-called defenseless players. However, Travis Kelce has suggested no player should be defenseless when on the field in such a physical game. There are some real concerns over the direction of the game with calls like this being made.
